summary.oneLiner: Shaily delivered 34% revenue growth and 1,030 bps EBITDA margin expansion driven by explosive 163% growth in Healthcare segment, now 38% of revenue, as its next-gen Axiom Max GLP-1 pen gains traction and capacity expands to 80M pens by FY26 end — this structural shift from commodity plastics to high-margin, IP-led device manufacturing is redefining its valuation multiple and creating a durable moat.

one-line thesis: Shaily delivered 34% revenue growth and 1,030 bps EBITDA margin expansion driven by explosive 163% growth in Healthcare segment, now 38% of revenue, as its next-gen Axiom Max GLP-1 pen gains traction and capacity expands to 80M pens by FY26 end — this structural shift from commodity plastics to high-margin, IP-led device manufacturing is redefining its valuation multiple and creating a durable moat.
financial scorecard: revenue: +34% YoY (INR257cr); EBITDA: +100% YoY to INR82cr, margin +1,030 bps to 31.8%; PAT: +134% YoY to INR51cr, margin +860 bps to 20%; order book: 4 new GLP-1 projects signed; net debt: debt-to-equity 0.3x, no net debt build reported
guidance: revenue growth: Healthcare segment to grow 30-40% annually; margin: sustained at current levels with upside as IP-led mix increases; order inflow: 4 new GLP-1 projects; capex/commissioning: INR125cr FY26 capex to expand capacity from 40M to 80M pens; line operational by end-Q3 FY26
order book & pipeline: 4 new GLP-1 projects signed; 5 new consumer projects with existing marquee customers; 1 new industrial project with automotive major
segment / subsidiary detail: Healthcare: INR99cr (38% of rev, +163% YoY); Consumer: INR135cr (-3% YoY); Industrial: INR23cr (+45% YoY); Exports: 68% of revenue; 19 new machines installed; capacity expanding from 40M to 80M pens by FY26 end
growth verticals / optionality: Consumer Electronics: commercial supply to begin H2 FY26; semiconductor component opportunity under active development; potential for $20M-$100M business in 3-5 years; U.K. innovation unit expanding into patch pumps and on-body injectors
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expanded due to higher mix of IP-led devices (Axiom Max, Neo) with better gross margins; cost leverage from scale; no material input cost inflation cited; margin sustainability supported by product mix shift
capex / expansion: INR125cr allocated in FY26 for Healthcare capacity expansion (40M → 80M pens); small marginal capex for Consumer Electronics; no major capex planned for Dubai or UK subsidiary currently
capital allocation: 94,500 stock options granted to employees; debt-to-equity at 0.3x; ROCE 42.3%, ROE 32.7%; capital disciplined, no dividend policy mentioned
risks & watch-items: regulatory delays in Canada (mitigated by multi-customer diversification); Chinese competition in low-end markets; potential supply chain disruption if customer launches delayed >12 months; consumer electronics and semiconductor bets unproven
management quality / tone: highly confident, strategic, and forward-looking; emphasized IP moat, scalability, and global pharma partnerships; transparent on guidance limitations but clear on directional momentum
non-obvious takeaways: Axiom Max’s design eliminates priming and includes dose counter — a rare innovation in GLP-1 pens; 18 dedicated meetings at global expos indicate strong innovator interest beyond generics; 68% export ratio suggests deep global integration despite being an Indian SME

themes.driver: Export (US/EU/tariff) + Make-in-India import-substitution and product/capex cycle.
